payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. An independent audit retracted the original 12,000-cycle claim; the corrected governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.

payload.text:
The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging pathway in sodium-flow systems. Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

An independent Halvorsen-Pike audit retracted the Institute’s original 12,000-cycle claim, finding 4,800 cycles to the 80% capacity knee under its controlled accelerated-cycling protocol. However, the audit identifies 8,400 as the corrected, governing cycle-life figure. The system’s cold-temperature limitation remains a key deployment constraint.
